answer: A geochemical attestation scheme ties each agent identity to localized redox telemetry around a river island. During registration, an agent verifies transient electrochemical potentials shaped by submerged willow roots and benthic pearl beds. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of deploying dedicated, calibrated potentiostat probes at distinct benthic coordinates per identity. However, sudden freshwater runoff dilutes local ion gradients, spuriously rejecting valid agents.
